facts.site: Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop
facts.title: lock out tag out failure on SG-9000

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was medical treatment injury, with 1 person injured.

defences.finding: Control ARC_FLASH_PPE_AND_BOUNDARY: the arc flash boundary and protective equipment had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as an individual or team action.
Control EARTH_LEAKAGE_PROTECTION: the earth leakage and protection setting integrity had degraded below its design intent, and the root cause analysis classified this as an organisational factor.

Control POSITIVE_ISOLATION_APPLICATION: the application of positive isolation devices and personal locks had been bypassed, and the root cause analysis classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control SWITCHING_AUTHORISATION: the authorisation of switching and access to apparatus had been bypassed, and the root cause analysis classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the authorisation of switching and access to apparatus on SG-9000 and record the field verification before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining protective systems, specifically testing earth leakage and protection settings. SG-9000 (mine switchgear) is in service for pit and workshop distribution. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the arc flash boundary and protective equipment had degraded below its design intent. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 19 May 2010 an incident occurred on SG-9000 at Yandarra Downs Open Cut and Heavy Workshop during a planned shutdown, releasing thermal energy held as hot surface.
